question.value: What is the physical, kinematical, and chemical structure of the massive protostellar hot core Mon R2 IRS 3 at high spatial resolution?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we use ALMA observations to probe the physical and chemical structure of the Mon R 2 IRS 3 hot core, that is located in the Monoceros R2 giant molecular cloud.

Based on high spatial resolution continuum and spectroscopic ALMA observations, in the following we investigate the kinematics (Sect. 3.3) and chemistry (Sect. 4) of this massive protostar that is a reference for massive star formation studies.
The observations were performed on April 2015 within the project 2015.1.00453.S.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO. 2016.1.00813.S.
We used the Band 6 receiver in two different tunings corresponding to two different science goals
We have constructed continuum images at 1.2mm and 1.1mm by averaging the channels free from line emission in each band

analysis_steps.goal: Extract spectra and identify molecular lines

method.value: Extract interferometric spectra towards IRS 3 A and IRS 3 B and identify transitions above 4 sigma integrated intensity using CDMS and JPL spectroscopic catalogs.

evidence.quote: To study the chemical content of IRS 3, we have extracted the interferometric spectra towards IRS 3 A and IRS 3 B.

The lines have been identified using the $"$The Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy$"$ (CDMS) (cite: Muller2005; Endres2016) and the "Jet Propulsion Laboratory Line catalogue" (JPL) (cite: Pickett1998). We have adopted the 4$\sigma$ level in integrated intensity as the detection limit.

evidence.quote: We have adopted the 4$\sigma$ level in integrated intensity as the detection limit.

We have checked the identification of the S-bearing species by searching for the $^{34}$S isotopologues to test that the (non-)detections of all the $^{34}$S isotopologues are compatible with a standard ratio of $^{32}$S/$^{34}$S=22.5 (cite: Wilson1994; Chin1996).

validation.value: Checked S-bearing species against 34S isotopologues assuming 32S/34S = 22.5; confirmed CH3OCH3 detection using LTE synthetic spectrum at T_ex = 170 K

evidence.quote: We have checked the identification of the S-bearing species by searching for the $^{34}$S isotopologues to test that the (non-)detections of all the $^{34}$S isotopologues are compatible with a standard ratio of $^{32}$S/$^{34}$S=22.5 (cite: Wilson1994; Chin1996).

In order to confirm (reject) this detection, we produced a synthetic spectrum assuming Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium and T$_{ex}$=170 K and checked that the obtained spectrum is compatible with the observed spectra

analysis_steps.goal: Analyze spatial distribution and gas kinematics using moment maps and PV diagrams

method.value: Compute zeroth-moment (integrated intensity) and first-moment (intensity-weighted velocity) maps, and extract Position-Velocity (PV) diagrams perpendicular to and along the reflection nebula axis to compare with Keplerian and solid-body rotation curves.

evidence.quote: The integrated intensity maps (zeroth-moment maps) of the most intense lines are shown in Fig. 3.
Relevant information on the structure and kinematics of the molecular gas can also be obtained from the first-moment maps shown in Fig. 5.

To further explore the kinematics of the molecular gas and distinguish between a toroidal envelope from the circumstellar disk, we have performed Position-Velocity (PV) diagrams in the direction perpendicular to the reflection nebula ("toroid" in Figs. 5b).

findings_qualitative.value: The 1.1mm continuum resolves two components, IRS 3 A and IRS 3 B, separated by ~0.65", with IRS 3 A containing ~80% of the continuum flux and hosting the hot core.

evidence.quote: The continuum image at 1.1mm shows two components, IRS 3 A and IRS 3 B, that are separated by $\sim$0.65$"$. We estimate that IRS 3 A is responsible of $\sim$80 % of the continuum flux, being the most massive component.
The COMs CH$_3$OCHO and CH$_3$OCH$_3$ are only detected towards IRS 3 A proving that the hot core is associated to this protostar.

findings_qualitative.value: Chemical spatial differentiation is present around IRS 3 A: most species peak within R<0.3" of IRS 3 A, COMs (CH3OCHO) and H2CS peak ~0.5" SW in the southern NIR nebula, and HC3N peaks ~0.5" NE.

evidence.quote: Most of the observed species peak in a region R$<$0.3" from IRS 3 A.

The peak of the CH$_3$OCHO is located $\sim$0.5$"$ SW to IRS 3 A-mm, that is about a half of the HPBW of our observations. The peak of the HC$_3$N emission is displaced by $\sim$0.5$"$ NE from IRS 3 A-mm.

findings_qualitative.value: First-moment maps and PV diagrams show a SE-NW velocity gradient (7-11 km s^-1) perpendicular to the NIR reflection nebula, consistent with a rotating ring/toroid or unresolved circumstellar disk.

evidence.quote: Most of the first-moment maps present a clear SE-NW velocity gradient in the v$_{lsr}$=7$-$11 km s$^{-1}$ velocity range.
The detected velocity gradient is consistent with the emission coming from a toroidal envelope and/or a disk that is rotating in the direction perpendicular to the axis defined by the NIR nebula

findings_qualitative.value: SO2 is the most abundant gas-phase S-bearing molecule detected (~1.3x10^-7), accounting for ~1% of the solar sulphur budget, implying >95% of sulphur remains locked in refractories or unobservable species like sulphur allotropes.

evidence.quote: Following our calculations, SO$_2$ accounts for a significant fraction, $\sim$1%, of the sulphur budget. The abundance of SO$_2$ is a factor $>$5 higher than those of SO, OCS, and H$_2$CS. This implies that $>$95% of the sulphur should be locked in refractories or species such as S$_2$ and sulphur allotropes that cannot be observed.

claims.hypothesis: Mon R2 IRS 3 is composed of multiple millimeter components and the hot core is associated with a specific member of the mini-cluster.
claims.experiment: Image 1.1 mm and 1.2 mm continuum with Briggs robust=0.5, fit 2D Gaussians, and extract molecular spectra towards the resolved continuum peaks IRS 3 A and IRS 3 B.
claims.result: Two continuum sources separated by ~0.65" are resolved; IRS 3 A accounts for ~80% of the flux and exhibits crowded spectra with COMs (CH3OCHO, CH3OCH3) that are absent towards IRS 3 B.
claims.finding: The hot core in Mon R2 IRS 3 is specifically associated with the more massive millimeter component IRS 3 A.

evidence.quote: The continuum image at 1.1mm shows two components, IRS 3 A and IRS 3 B, that are separated by $\sim$0.65$"$. We estimate that IRS 3 A is responsible of $\sim$80 % of the continuum flux, being the most massive component.
The COMs CH$_3$OCHO and CH$_3$OCH$_3$ are only detected towards IRS 3 A proving that the hot core is associated to this protostar.

claims.hypothesis: The molecular gas around IRS 3 A is organized into distinct kinematic and chemical components (rotating toroid/disk vs. outflow cavity walls).
claims.experiment: Construct 0th and 1st moment maps and extract PV diagrams perpendicular and parallel to the NIR reflection nebula axis for detected molecular transitions.
claims.result: Most molecules peak within 0.3" of IRS 3 A and show a SE-NW velocity gradient (7-11 km s^-1) perpendicular to the NIR nebula matching solid-body/Keplerian rotation, whereas CH3OCHO peaks ~0.5" SW in the southern nebula without the rotation gradient, and HC3N peaks ~0.5" NE.
claims.finding: Most molecular emission arises from a rotating ring/toroid or unresolved disk around IRS 3 A, while CH3OCHO traces the walls of the outflow-excavated cavity in the southern NIR nebula.

evidence.quote: The kinematical study suggests that the molecular emission is mainly coming from a rotating ring and/or an unresolved disk. Additional components are traced by the ro-vibrational HCN $\nu_2$=1 3$\rightarrow$2 line which is probing the inner disk/jet region, and the weak lines of CH$_3$OCHO, more likely arising from the walls of the cavity excavated by the molecular outflow.
Most of the first-moment maps present a clear SE-NW velocity gradient in the v$_{lsr}$=7$-$11 km s$^{-1}$ velocity range.

claims.hypothesis: Evaporation of icy grain mantles in the hot core releases the bulk of elemental sulphur into observable gas-phase S-bearing species dominated by SO2.
claims.experiment: Derive rotation temperatures and LTE column densities of SO2, 34SO2, SO, OCS, OC34S, and H2CS towards IRS 3 A and compare total gas-phase sulphur abundance to the solar sulphur abundance (S/H = 1.5x10^-5).
claims.result: T_rot(SO2) = 175 (+15/-16) K, X(SO2) ~ 1.3x10^-7 (over 5 times more abundant than SO, OCS, and H2CS), X(SO/SO2) ~ 0.29, and all detected S-bearing molecules account for only ~1% of solar sulphur.
claims.finding: SO2 is the main observable gas-phase sulphur reservoir in IRS 3 A, released primarily by radiative heating (or mild shocks), but >95% of elemental sulphur remains locked in refractory material or unobservable allotropes.

evidence.quote: Our results are therefore more consistent with the interpretation that sulphur has been released from the ices due to radiative heating (or perhaps mild shocks) rather than sputtered by strong shocks.

Following our calculations, SO$_2$ accounts for a significant fraction, $\sim$1%, of the sulphur budget. The abundance of SO$_2$ is a factor $>$5 higher than those of SO, OCS, and H$_2$CS. This implies that $>$95% of the sulphur should be locked in refractories or species such as S$_2$ and sulphur allotropes that cannot be observed.

why_this_data.value: Previous single-dish and lower-resolution interferometric observations could not resolve the individual members of the Mon R2 IRS 3 mini-cluster, requiring high spatial and spectral resolution (<0.3 km s^-1) ALMA observations.

evidence.quote: All the mm studies carried out. thus far towards IRS 3 were performed with single-dish observations or interferometric observations which are unable to resolve the IRS 3 mini-cluster (see (cite: Boonmanvd2003; vandertak2003; Dierickx2015).
A total of 18 spectral windows were observed, each with a spectral resolution $<$0.3 km s$^{-1}$ which allows to fully resolve the profiles of the detected lines

why_this_method.value: Briggs weighting (robust=0.5) was used for continuum to achieve higher spatial resolution, natural weighting for lines to maximize sensitivity, and LTE/rotational diagrams because high hot core densities (n(H2) > 10^7 cm^-3) thermalize the transitions.

evidence.quote: Spectroscopic images of all spectral windows were produced in CASA using natural weighting. In the case of the higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) continuum images, we used Briggs weighting (robust=0.5) to achieve higher spatial resolution.

The molecular column densities of the rest of species have been derived by fitting the lines observed towards IRS 3 A assuming Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE), which is a reasonable assumption for the high densities (n(H$_2$)$>$10$^7$ cm$^{-3}$) expected in a hot core.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Fitting SO2 and CH3OH lines with multiple rotation temperatures was rejected due to the small number of observed transitions.

evidence.quote: Given the small number of transitions observed, we do not consider that we could obtain realistic results using a more complex fitting with several rotation temperatures.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Strong shock sputtering as the primary origin of gas-phase SO2 was rejected in favor of radiative heating (or mild shocks) because SO2 lines are narrow (~4 km s^-1) and follow the toroid PV pattern.

evidence.quote: However, the SO$_2$ lines toward Mon R 2 IRS 3 A are substantially narrow $\Delta V \sim$ 4 km s$^{-1}$, compared with the high velocities observed in the bipolar outflow detected by (cite: Dierickx2015).

Our results are therefore more consistent with the interpretation that sulphur has been released from the ices due to radiative heating (or perhaps mild shocks) rather than sputtered by strong shocks.

limitations_admitted.value: The angular resolution (~1.2" x 0.9" for lines, ~0.95" x 0.63" for 1.1mm continuum) barely resolves IRS 3 A and B, cannot separate NIR sources B and C, cannot resolve HCN v2=1 emission, and cannot distinguish an unresolved Keplerian disk from a solid-body rotating ring.

evidence.quote: The angular resolution of the 1.1mm image is not enough to cleanly discern between IRS 3 B and IRS 3 A.

In the cases of unresolved disks, where the sensitivity is not enough to detect the highest rotation velocities expected close to the star, a Keplerian disk and solid-body rotation would be difficult to differentiate.
Given that the emission of the HCN $\nu_2$=1 is not resolved, we could not disentangle between these two physical processes.

limitations_admitted.value: Interferometric observations filter out extended emission, causing absorption and negative contours in C2H and HNC and missed flux signatures in HCN, H13CN, and SO.

evidence.quote: It should be noticed that our observations are filtering the extended emission, thus producing negative contours in the emission of these molecules also far from the compact hot core. Signatures of missed flux are also found in the HCN 3$\rightarrow$2, H$^{13}$CN 3$\rightarrow$2, and to a lesser extent in the SO 6$_6$$\rightarrow$5$_5$ and 7$_6$$\rightarrow$6$_5$ images.

limitations_admitted.value: A single rotation temperature cannot fit all observed SO2 or CH3OH lines well because of a steep temperature gradient along the line of sight.

evidence.quote: However, we do not obtain a good fit to the three millimeter lines observed, which is the consequence of the steep gas temperature gradient along the line of sight (see Figs. 7). We cannot obtain a good fit to all the methanol lines using a single rotation temperature, either.

limitations_admitted.value: Lines of abundant species like CH3OH, HCN, and SO (and possibly CH3OCHO) may be optically thick, making derived abundances lower limits and affecting abundance ratios.

evidence.quote: We recall that the CH$_3$OH lines are very likely optically thick and the derived abundance a lower limit to the real value.

One possibility is that the CH$_3$OCHO lines are optically thick and we are underestimating their column densities. Another possibility is that the N(SO)/N(SO$_2$) ratio is overestimated because the SO lines are optically thick, and the hot core is in an earlier evolutionary stage.

limitations_admitted.value: Lack of interferometric observations of H2S and CS prevents a complete inventory of gas-phase S-bearing molecules.

evidence.quote: We do not have interferometric observations of the abundant species, H$_2$S and CS, that would be useful to complete the inventory of S-bearing molecules.

referee_caveats_inferred: There is a discrepancy in the reported ALMA project code: Section 2 states 2015.1.00453.S (matching the ALMA archive manifest), whereas the Acknowledgements state ADS/JAO. 2016.1.00813.S.
There is a minor discrepancy in N(CH3OH): the text in Section 4 gives 1.1(+0.3/-0.2) x 10^17 cm^-2, while Table 2 lists 1.4 x 10^17 cm^-2.
The spectral index alpha = 3.7 +/- 3.3 is derived over a very narrow lever arm (1.1 mm vs 1.2 mm) and has an uncertainty nearly equal to the value itself.

In Table 2, the column density of HCN (1.1x10^15 cm^-2 at 170 K) is only ~3.7 times higher than H13CN (3.0x10^14 cm^-2), confirming severe optical depth in the main HCN 3-2 line, yet Table 2 lists the uncorrected main-line HCN abundance (4.2x10^-9) while the text in Section 4 states that HCN has an abundance of a few 10^-7.
